description: Independent cross-capability check of the baseline OpenSpec specs (the Cross-check phase of spec-pipeline on its own), plus verification that previously reported findings are resolved.

gaps: NFR-9 (cross-cutting, admin half) is effectively owned only by content-authoring. The only externalization check, content-authoring:605-614 'Externalized admin strings', renders only 'the source list, task editor, mission editor and preview'. Other admin UI is English but has no externalization requirement in any spec: the sign-in form (admin-access:73-77, 'Admin UI copy is English' at admin-access:23), the stats page and the flag queue (progress-stats:11). The deliberate exclusion list covers only the child-UI half of NFR-9, so this admin half is silently partial. Either widen the content-authoring scenario to every admin screen, or list admin-UI externalization outside authoring as a Phase 3 owner item.

Traceability defect in content-authoring:42 (CA-D20 justification). It reads 'answer-checking..answer-checking: admin and child notation then agree'. This looks like a stale or garbled requirement-range reference and does not point at a resolvable requirement. It should name the answer-checking requirements it means (e.g. 'Numeric notation', 'Decimal input').
contradictions: Oversized child request body: the status code is inconsistent. practice-flow:343-346 (requirement text) says the API SHALL refuse with HTTP 400 '... and any child request body over 16 KB'. practice-flow's own scenario 'Request body too large' (practice-flow:387-391) requires HTTP 413 for a body over 16 KB. answer-checking:875-877 also lists 'oversized request bodies' among the HTTP 400 cases. The specs disagree on 400 vs 413. Pick one (413 is the conventional status) and align practice-flow:346 and answer-checking:876 with it.

Expected-value range: content-authoring vs practice-flow. content-authoring:420-421 (CA-D20, line 42) and its scenario at content-authoring:466-470 refuse to save any numeric expected value with absolute value ≥ 10^12, explicitly including `99999999999999999999`. practice-flow:375-379 ('Huge integer that is the expected answer') requires a stored, child-served INTEGER part 'expecting `100000000000000000000`'. An admin cannot author that, so the practice-flow e2e scenario is unreachable. answer-checking:156-160 uses the same kind of value, but there it is a pure-checker or golden case and does not depend on stored content, so it is not in conflict. Fix: change practice-flow:375-379 to an expected value below 10^12 with a submitted value written with grouping separators (e.g. `999 999 999 999` vs expected `999999999999`), or state there that the part is seeded directly, bypassing authoring validation.

deferred: NFR-9 externalization of child UI strings, and of admin UI strings outside the authoring screens (sign-in, stats, flag queue)
NFR-10 Docker volume and cross-platform backup command
NFR-11 module boundaries verified by tests
NFR-12 contract drift check in the build
NFR-13 WCAG AA contrast and reduced motion for screens outside gamification, including the admin UI
NFR-3 PII scope beyond the display name (report notes, answers in logs, recordings)
NFR-4 copyright scope beyond authoring fixtures (golden table, seeded e2e content, skin assets)

contradictions: CHOICE_SINGLE with several accepted keys: content-authoring vs answer-checking. content-authoring:435 (Answer spec authoring table, CHOICE_SINGLE row) requires 'exactly one option marked correct'. The same row refuses 'more than one correct option', and the scenario 'Invalid single-choice spec' at content-authoring:520-524 refuses options A and B both marked correct. answer-checking:572-573 ('Accepted alternatives': 'For CHOICE_SINGLE every accepted key is an alternative') and its scenario 'Single choice with two accepted keys' at answer-checking:593-597 (accepted keys A and D, input D gives CORRECT) define checker behavior for a spec that authoring forbids. That checker scenario is also a mandatory golden case (answer-checking:832-834). Under FR-20 ('A part can list several accepted alternatives') the content-authoring rule is a narrowing. Yet no derived decision in the CA-D table (content-authoring:21-43) records it, unlike the other narrowings (CA-D3, CA-D4, CA-D13). Fix: either add a CA-D decision that narrows FR-20 for CHOICE_SINGLE and drop or reframe answer-checking:572-573/593-597, or let content-authoring accept several correct options for CHOICE_SINGLE.

previousFindings.evidence: The deliberate-exclusion list now names 'NFR-9 externalization of ... admin UI strings outside the authoring screens (sign-in, stats, flag queue)' as a Phase 3 owner item, so the admin half is no longer silently partial. content-authoring:605-614 still scopes its check to 'the source list, task editor, mission editor and preview' (line 613), which matches that split. No other spec contradicts it: admin-access:23 ('Admin UI copy is English') and progress-stats:11 ('the admin UI is English') only state the language and claim no externalization ownership.

content-authoring:42 (CA-D20 justification) now reads 'answer-checking (integer, decimal, fraction and unit input): admin and child notation then agree, ...'. This resolves to the answer-checking requirements 'Integer input' (answer-checking:168), 'Decimal input' (:221), 'Fraction input' (:263) and 'Numbers with units' (:361). The garbled 'answer-checking..answer-checking' range is gone.

practice-flow:342-347 now says the API refuses only malformed request shapes with HTTP 400, and that 'Any child request body over 16 KB SHALL be refused with HTTP 413 (the contract's `TooLarge` response)'. This matches its scenario 'Request body too large' at practice-flow:388-392 (413). answer-checking:875-877 now reads 'Malformed request shapes ... are HTTP 400 and request bodies over 16 KB are HTTP 413'. All three places agree on 413. child-profile:321-326 (a 10,240-character locale value gives 400) stays under 16 KB, so it does not conflict.

practice-flow:376-380 ('Huge integer that is the expected answer') now expects `999999999999`, explicitly 'the largest value an admin can author, content-authoring CA-D20', and submits `999 999 999 999` with no-break spaces. That value is below 10^12, so content-authoring:420-421 and :466-470 accept it, and the scenario is reachable. The remaining huge-number cases do not need authored content: practice-flow:370-374 expects `12` and only submits a huge input, and answer-checking:156-160 is a pure checker/golden case.
